jobs.prompt: Owner bug: the oasis project has 1,750 swarm worktrees (167 GB), some from Sep 21: swarm leaks run worktrees. Required: (A) CLEANUP AFTER A RUN: when a run is integrated (integrateRun and the queue path), cancelled, or abandoned (failed or timed-out and left untouched), the swarm removes THAT run worktrees and workspaces: for each job workspace under state.worktreesBase (see worktreesBaseFor in tools/swarm/core-11.mjs, tools/swarm.mjs line about 492 and 735, job workspaces under .swarm/workspaces/RUN/JOB and git worktrees created with git worktree add --detach): git worktree remove --force, git worktree prune, rm the directory, then remove the empty run folder under the base. Safety: never remove while any job of the run is running or a process of the run is alive; only after integration has recorded integratedFiles and hashes (or the run is cancelled/abandoned); never touch paths outside the known bases (the repo .swarm/workspaces and the worktrees base resolved for this repo); keep results needed for retry of a PARTIAL integration (blocked jobs of a partial run keep their workspaces until the run is fully integrated or cancelled); every removal is logged in the run journal (path, bytes freed). A config switch keepWorkspaces (profile or local config, default false) and a flag --keep-workspaces on run/integrate disable it. (B) swarm gc: a new command, module tools/gc.mjs, wired into the CLI dispatch (find how commands such as cancel and orphans are dispatched), usage text, tools/watch-command-meta.mjs and tools/completion.mjs so completion tests pass. swarm gc [--apply] [--all-projects | --root PATH] [--older-than DAYS (default 7)] [--keep-runs N (default 20 newest run folders per project)] [--include-scratch] [--json]. DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: prints a table of what it would remove with bytes: (1) worktrees and workspaces of finished runs (integrated, cancelled, or failed/timeout older than DAYS) found via each project .swarm/runs/*/state.json and the worktrees base; (2) ORPHANS: git worktree list entries whose directory is gone (git worktree prune), directories under a worktrees base that belong to no run state, older than DAYS; (3) old run folders .swarm/runs/RUN older than DAYS beyond the N newest (state.json and the journal are kept as a small summary file runs/RUN/summary.json before the heavy folders go); (4) with --include-scratch: stale scratch projects under the scratch base (~/.project-swarm-scratch and the OS temp folders matching swarm test or tmp prefixes) older than DAYS that are not registered real projects and are not git worktrees of the current repo with unpushed commits (check git status and unpushed branch commits: never remove a worktree whose branch has commits not on any remote or has uncommitted changes unless --force-unsafe is passed and then say so). --apply removes with a final line freed bytes; it refuses to run when a swarm run is active in that project (pid alive) and skips that project with a reason. All projects mode reads the projects registry (tools/projects.mjs listProjects with includeScratch) and never follows symlinks out of known bases (realpath checks). Never delete anything outside .swarm, the worktrees base and the scratch base; never delete the main checkout; log to a gc log file. JSON output has per-category counts and bytes and a total, plus diskUsage: { projects: [{root, worktrees, workspaces, runFolders, bytes}], totalBytes }, computed with a bounded fast size walk (du -sk when available, with a time limit and a cached value in .swarm/disk-usage.json refreshed at most every 10 minutes) so the board can show it. (C) Provide the board contract only (do not edit board files, another seat owns them): swarm gc --json --usage prints just diskUsage. (D) Tests in tests/gc.test.mjs and tests/run-cleanup.test.mjs, hermetic (temp git repo with real git worktree add, temp base, injected clock via file mtimes, no ambient environment): integrated run worktrees are removed and logged, a partial run keeps the blocked job workspace, a running run is untouched, keepWorkspaces keeps everything, dry run lists and removes nothing, apply removes finished and orphan worktrees and prunes git metadata, active run project skipped, worktree with unpushed commits survives without --force-unsafe, paths outside the bases are never touched even if a state file points there, symlink escape refused, old run folders beyond N removed with summary kept, JSON usage shape, completion test passes. Keep every existing integrate, cancel and run test passing (run the files with integrate, cancel, completion, orphans, workspace in the name). ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.
